Olá, pessoal! Vamos construir uma missão espacial juntos?

Sou, entusiasta de tecnologia, inovação e empreendedorismo. Tenho experiência no desenvolvimento de soluções digitais, simuladores, dashboards e sistemas inteligentes, com projetos envolvendo automação, inteligência artificial, sustentabilidade.Nossa ideia é desenvolver o LUNAR COMMAND, um jogo educativo e interativo no qual jovens administram uma base lunar, enfrentando desafios relacionados à energia, oxigênio, alimentação,radiação.
summary:
ZUNO is a browser game for kids ages 7–12 in which they take care of Zuno, an alien astronaut dog stranded on the Moon, and keep his lunar base alive until they repair his rocket. Every action is a real mission trade-off: exploring the Moon collects scrap but costs oxygen and energy; extracting ice gives water but costs energy; planting costs water and energy today and becomes food days later; sleeping restores energy and oxygen but ends the day. No choice is free. 

The rules come from real NASA open data. Plant yields come from the EDEN ISS space greenhouse study (NASA OSDR, OSD-895). Growth times come from vegetables grown in Apollo 14 lunar soil (OSD-883). Exploration costs are based on real lunar terrain measured by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO/LOLA). The game runs on any phone or computer with no download or account. It has read-aloud narration, difficulty levels by age, and a daily screen-time limit for parents.
details:
WHAT IT DOES ZUNO

Turns the core challenge of a lunar outpost — balancing life support, power, water and food — into a virtual-pet game. Players manage three resources that are always visible: Energy, Oxygen and Scrap. Water appears in the greenhouse.

THE GAME LOOP (every choice has a cost)

• Explore: gain scrap; spend oxygen and energy. If oxygen runs out on the way back, a robot rescues Zuno but half of the backpack is lost.

• Extract ice: gain water; spend energy. • Plant: spend water and energy now; harvest food days later.

• Harvest: food becomes energy for Zuno.

• Sleep: restores energy and oxygen and makes plants grow, but advances the mission day. Zuno also uses energy over time, so doing nothing has a cost too.

• Upgrade: spend scrap on a bigger oxygen tank, more greenhouse domes and the 5 rocket parts. Pipe and wire mini-games add variety. The last rocket parts need a bigger tank, so players must plan ahead.

HOW NASA DATA DRIVES THE RULES

• NASA OSDR OSD-895 (EDEN ISS greenhouse, Antarctica 2018): real harvested biomass of cucumber, lettuce and radish sets how much energy each harvest gives (10 + kg × 0.35). Cucumber's continuous “spread harvest” lets it be harvested 3 times.

• NASA OSDR OSD-883 (vegetables grown in Apollo 14 lunar soil): real days to harvest (lettuce 18, radish 14) set in-game growth time (real days ÷ 7, scaled by difficulty). Cucumber cycle time is an estimate and is labelled “estimate” in the game.

• LRO / LOLA (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, via NASA Moon Trek): the elevation model is read pixel by pixel to compute the average altitude and slope of 16 zones around Copernicus Crater and Fra Mauro (Apollo 14 landing site). Slope and distance set the oxygen/energy cost of each exploration site; slope and low altitude set how much scrap is found.

• An in-game “NASA Data” panel lists every source with links. Data is fetched live through a small proxy and cached. When offline, the game uses embedded values taken from the same studies and clearly shows “OFFLINE”, so static data is never presented as live.

ACCESSIBILITY AND FAMILIES

• Plays in the browser on phone or desktop; no download, no account.

• Every text has a read-aloud button, plus a guiding robot. Portuguese and English.

• Three difficulty levels by age: 7–8, 9–10, 11–12.

• Parental supervision mode, protected by a multiplication question: a daily screen-time limit (15–90 min). When time is up, Zuno goes to sleep and invites the child to come back tomorrow, with progress saved, so the session ends with a story instead of a fight.

IMPACT

Kids leave understanding a real constraint of deep-space survival: every resource you spend today is one you don't have tomorrow. Families get purposeful screen time with limits, and teachers can use it in class with just a link.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (no framework); Node.js server for local play; Vercel serverless functions as a proxy and cache for the NASA APIs; Web Speech API for narration; Google Fonts (Fredoka, Lilita One).

CREATIVITY

Instead of a dashboard, the outpost is a pet you care about. The emotional bond with Zuno makes trade-offs matter to young players, and failure is never punitive: the robot rescues Zuno and players try a different strategy.

NEXT STEPS

Add real space weather (NASA DONKI) for radiation events and base shielding; Spanish version; a classroom pilot in Caxias do Sul, Brazil.

SI USE

AI coding assistants helped write parts of the code. [Character art, screen art and intro/ending videos were generated with AI image/video tools and are marked “AI-generated”.] All NASA data is real and cited in the in-game “NASA Data” panel.
